items.title: The Seventh and Final Numeric Category Opens: The Seven Factors of Enlightenment, Sorted Into Calm, Insight, and What Runs Through Both

items.zh: 已說六種佛教所應知處。次說七種。謂有七法，能於諸諦如實覺了，圓滿解脫。謂毘鉢舍那品有三，一、擇法，二、精進，三、喜。奢摩他品亦有三，一、安，二、三摩地，三、捨。念、通二品。
items.en: The six-thing category of what a Buddhist should know has now been explained. Next, the seven-thing category. There are seven things capable of genuinely awakening to the truths and bringing full liberation: the insight group has three — discrimination of phenomena, diligence, and joy; the calm group likewise has three — pliancy, concentration, and equanimity; and mindfulness runs through both groups at once.

items.title: Seven Kinds of Noble Person Sorted by Faculty, Fruit, and Liberation, and the Eightfold Path Reorganized Into Three Causes of Concentration

items.zh: 又由根故、果故、解脫故，建立七種補特伽羅。於向道中，依鈍根、利根故，建立隨信、隨法行。於果道中，即此二種，名信解脫見到。定障解脫，非煩惱障解脫故，建立身證；煩惱障解脫，非定障解脫故，建立慧解脫；定障、煩惱障俱解脫故，建立俱分解脫。又三因緣七種行故，令修行者心得內定，心正一緣。謂趣入、安住、攝受因緣。若世間正見，了知定有施與等行，及此為依，了知居家迫迮、居家塵染等行，出離所引正思惟，名趣入因緣。既趣入已，受持正語、正業、正命，名安住因緣。於趣入因緣、安住因緣，及後方便作意隨行中所有正精進、正念、名攝受因緣。
items.en: By faculty, by fruit, and by liberation, seven kinds of person are established. Within the path towards the fruit, by dull or sharp faculty, one who follows through faith and one who follows through the teaching are established. Within the fruit itself, these same two are named one of confident faith and one who has arrived at seeing. Liberation from the obstruction of concentration, but not from the obstruction of affliction, establishes the witness-with-the-body; liberation from the obstruction of affliction, but not from the obstruction of concentration, establishes the wisdom-liberated; liberation from both obstructions establishes the both-liberated. By three causal conditions comprising seven practices, a practitioner's mind attains inward concentration, rightly fixed on a single object: the causal conditions of entering, of abiding, and of being sustained. Worldly right view — knowing with certainty that giving and the rest are real — taken as a basis, together with knowing the confinement and defilement of household life, and right intention drawn from renunciation, is called the causal condition of entering. Having entered, upholding right speech, right action, and right livelihood is called the causal condition of abiding. Right diligence and right mindfulness, present throughout the causal conditions of entering and abiding and in the subsequent means and attention that follow, are called the causal condition of being sustained.

items.title: The Seven Kinds of Noble Wealth No Amount of Worldly Wealth Can Buy, and the Seven Demonic Forces That Are Simply Their Absence

items.zh: 又諸世間樂求財者，為得樂故，雖樂積集一切凡財，而未能得七種聖財所生之樂。謂與信俱行清淨之樂；生於善趣所起之樂；顧自妙好，不行諸惡，無有追悔所生之樂；顧他誹毀，不行諸惡，無有追悔所生之樂；於法於義正解俱行所生之樂；後世資財無所匱乏所生之樂；於勝義諦如實覺悟所生之樂。諸如是等無量無邊無罪之樂，樂求積集世間財者皆所未得，惟得現法資財無匱所生有罪妄想之樂。又有七種魔惑品力。一、憎嫉聖教；二、現行能往惡趣惡行；三、樂習不顧自妙好障法；四、樂習不顧他誹毀障法；五、於善不善、有罪無罪、若劣若勝、若黑若白，及廣分別緣起法中，不能解了；六、慳垢弊心，積集眾具；七、智慧陜劣，愚癡增廣。若能降伏如是七種魔惑品力，當知即是聖法律中信等七力。
items.en: Worldly people who delight in seeking wealth, wishing to attain happiness, though they delight in accumulating every ordinary possession, are never able to attain the happiness born of the seven kinds of noble wealth: the pure happiness accompanying faith; the happiness arising from rebirth in a favourable destiny; the happiness born of, out of regard for one's own fine [future] state, not committing evil and having nothing to regret; the happiness born of, mindful of others' censure, not committing evil and having nothing to regret; the happiness accompanying correct understanding of the teaching and its meaning; the happiness born of never lacking resources in future lives; and the happiness born of genuinely awakening to the ultimate truth. There are also seven forces of Māra's affliction: hatred and envy towards the sacred teaching; committing conduct that leads towards the evil destinies; delighting in habits that disregard one's own fine [future] state; delighting in habits that disregard others' censure; being unable to understand wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright, and the full analysis of dependent origination; a mind fouled by the stain of stinginess, hoarding possessions; and narrow, inferior wisdom, with delusion ever spreading. If one is able to subdue these seven forces of Māra's affliction, know that this is precisely the seven powers — faith and the rest — within the sacred doctrine and discipline.

items.title: Seven Causes of the True Teaching's Decline, and Seven Causes of Its Enduring Flourishing

items.zh: 又有七種第一義法涅槃所對治法，能令正法衰退隱沒。如是七法、三衰損攝。謂受用衰損、增上意樂衰損、方便衰損。於衣服等樂求妙好，樂欲多求，及彼所起種種受用，名受用衰損。於道及道果涅槃心不信解，名增上意樂衰損。懈怠、失念、心亂、惡慧，名方便衰損。受用衰損，是貪不善根品類；意樂、方便衰損，是癡不善根品類。與此相違，當知即是白品七法。又有七種第一義法涅槃品法、能令正法無退久住。一、聞所成慧；二、思所成慧；三、修所成慧；四、不為惡緣侵損依止；五、正求財法；六、無增上慢；七、於可供養、不可供養補特伽羅，能善簡擇此可供養，此不可供養。
items.en: There are also seven things counteracting the ultimate truth of nirvāṇa, capable of causing the true teaching to decline and disappear. These seven things are comprised within three declines: the decline of enjoyment, the decline of superior aspiration, and the decline of means. Delighting in seeking excellent clothing and the rest, desiring ever more of it, and the various forms of enjoyment that follow, is called the decline of enjoyment. Lacking confidence and resolve towards the path and its fruit, nirvāṇa, is called the decline of superior aspiration. Laziness, forgetfulness, a scattered mind, and faulty discernment are called the decline of means. There are also seven things belonging to the ultimate truth of nirvāṇa, capable of causing the true teaching to endure without decline: first, wisdom born of hearing; second, wisdom born of reflection; third, wisdom born of cultivation; fourth, a basis not damaged by harmful circumstances; fifth, rightly seeking wealth and the teaching; sixth, freedom from false confidence; seventh, skilfully discerning which persons are worthy of offerings and which are not.

items.zh: 此中由聞慧故、於未了義能正解了；由思慧故，於未善決定義能善思惟；由修慧故，斷諸煩惱；由無惡緣侵損依止故，堪能修斷；正求財法故，速證通慧；無增上慢故，於下品所證不生喜足；能善揀擇補特伽羅故，於諸世智大福者等不樂親近，亦不供養，唯樂親近供養少欲者等。

blocks.text: The sevens, the last numbered category. Today includes the seven factors of awakening sorted into calm and insight, and two lists every Dharma community should read: seven causes of the true teaching's decline, and seven causes of its endurance.

The **seven factors of awakening** (七覺支) sorted: "The insight group has three: discrimination of phenomena, diligence, and joy; the calm group likewise has three: pliancy, concentration, and equanimity; mindfulness runs through both." This is the classical balancing instruction: when the mind is sluggish, arouse the insight factors; when agitated, the calm factors; mindfulness is always needed. Venerable Miào Jìng on equanimity as a factor: evenness of mind, uprightness of mind, and effortless abiding.

Seven kinds of noble person, sorted by faculty, fruit, and liberation: faith-follower and Dharma-follower; one resolved by faith and one attained by view; the body-witness; the one liberated by wisdom; and the one liberated both ways. Master Cháng Bǎi: liberation from the obstruction of concentration but not of affliction defines the body-witness, a non-returner who has attained cessation. Venerable Miào Jìng on the Dharma-follower: one who does only what is permissible by the Dharma.

subs.head: The eightfold path as cause of concentration

blocks.text: The eightfold path is reorganised into three causes of right concentration (Day 93). In "the mind rightly fixed on one object", Venerable Miào Jìng reads 正 as the object itself: the truth of cessation.

subs.head: Seven noble riches and seven forces of Māra

blocks.text: The seven noble riches (Day 31) cannot be bought. Their absence is Māra: faithlessness, broken precepts, shamelessness, lack of conscience, little learning, stinginess, and folly. Venerable Miào Jìng: "Māra here is one's own afflictions; they destroy one's merit; they delude oneself." The demon is internal.

subs.head: Why the Dharma declines, and why it endures

blocks.text: Seven causes of the true teaching's decline fall under three headings: decline in enjoyment of the Dharma, in aspiration (to the path and its fruit), and in means (laziness, forgetfulness, distraction, and folly), as Venerable Miào Jìng counts them. Seven causes make it endure. The *Pīxún jì* explains one, "a basis not damaged by harmful circumstances": avoiding the extreme of self-mortification, one eats enough to keep the body strong for practice.
The teaching lasts as long as practitioners keep it alive. These lists are less about history than about each community, and each person.

quiz.q: How does the treatise sort the seven factors of awakening into calm and insight?
options: discrimination, diligence, joy belong to insight; pliancy, concentration, equanimity to calm; mindfulness runs through both
quiz.why: "The insight group has three — discrimination of phenomena, diligence, and joy; the calm group likewise has three — pliancy, concentration, and equanimity; and mindfulness runs through both." Master Cháng Bǎi: mindfulness keeps the object unforgotten in either practice.

quiz.q: Per Venerable Miào Jìng, what three meanings make up equanimity as a factor of awakening?
options: evenness of mind, uprightness of mind, effortless abiding of mind
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Evenness of mind, uprightness of mind, effortless abiding of mind — having these three meanings is called equanimity." Master Cháng Bǎi: it is the balance of calming and uplifting.

quiz.q: "Liberation from the obstruction of concentration but not of affliction establishes the body-witness." Which fruit is this, per the lectures, and what does the note say?
options: the non-returner — attaining cessation, witnessed with the body; the note's "non-returner or arhat" is vague
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Liberated from the obstruction of concentration but not of affliction — this establishes the body-witness, that is, the third-fruit noble one." Venerable Miào Jìng: cessation is mindless, attained by the body, hence "body-witness."

quiz.q: How does the Pixunji derive the seven forces of Māra's affliction?
options: the reverse of the seven noble riches: faithlessness, broken precepts, shamelessness, lack of conscience, poor learning, stinginess, delusion
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: "These seven should be known as the reverse of the seven noble riches: faithlessness, broken precepts, shamelessness, lack of conscience, poor learning, stinginess, delusion — paired in order." Subduing them is the seven powers, faith and the rest.

quiz.q: What does Venerable Miào Jìng say "Māra" means here?
options: one's own afflictions, which destroy one's merit and delude oneself
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Māra here is one's own afflictions — one's own afflictions destroy one's merit; one's own afflictions delude oneself." Master Cháng Bǎi: all seven are the Māra of affliction, countered by faith, precepts, and the rest.

quiz.q: Seven things fall under three declines. How does Venerable Miào Jìng arrive at seven?
options: enjoyment is one; aspiration two — the path and its fruit; means four — laziness, forgetfulness, distraction, faulty discernment
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The second, decline of superior aspiration, has two: the path and the path's fruit." Master Cháng Bǎi lists the seven: discontent with robes, no confidence in the path, none in its fruit, laziness, forgetfulness, distraction, faulty discernment.

quiz.q: How does the Pixunji explain the fourth cause of endurance, "a basis not damaged by harmful circumstances"?
options: avoiding the extreme of self-mortification, taking food to sustain life, so the body is settled, strong, and able to cultivate severance
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: "Avoiding the extreme of self-mortification, one takes food and sustains life; the body abides at ease, free of hunger and weakness, strong and able, fit to cultivate severance." Master Cháng Bǎi: the true Dharma is both scriptural and realised.
